timeline.event: US legislation ended the quota-free status that had let garments of more than 50% ramie enter the United States outside textile import quotas.
Researchers reported enzymatic degumming of ramie bast fibers as an alternative to hot alkali treatment.
A study evaluated braided ramie fiber as a surgical suture biomaterial.
World ramie output was about 100,000 tonnes, below flax at about 310,000 tonnes, though ramie production value was higher than hemp or flax.
Structural analysis of ramie pectin was used to design a tailored enzyme cocktail for more efficient degumming.

timeline.event: Prato in Tuscany developed an industry regenerating carded wool from rags.
The US Wool Products Labeling Act required recycled wool to be disclosed separately from new wool.
Researchers used enzymes to digest wool out of wool and polyester blends and recover the polyester.
A mild acid process was reported for separating nylon 6 from wool carpet waste and regenerating its monomer.

timeline.event: Unifi launched REPREVE, a recycled polyester made from bottles and yarn waste.
Researchers including the company Carbios reported an engineered enzyme that depolymerized at least 90% of PET in 10 hours.
Recycled polyester reached about 8.9 million tonnes, about 12.5% of polyester fiber.
Recycled polyester rose to about 9.3 million tonnes, while its share of polyester fell to about 12%; about 98% still came from bottles.

timeline.event: The US Fur Products Labeling Act was enacted on 8 August, requiring fur labels to name the animal and country of origin.
The Truth in Fur Labeling Act (Public Law 111-313) was signed on 18 December, ending the exemption for items with less than 150 US dollars of fur.
From June to November, SARS-CoV-2 infected 290 Danish mink farms, mink-associated variants reached an estimated 4,000 people, and more than 15 million mink were culled.
California's AB 44 ban on selling and manufacturing new fur products took effect on 1 January.
An EFSA opinion found key welfare consequences of cage systems for mink could not be prevented or substantially mitigated within those systems.

timeline.event: Intensive farming of Arctic foxes began, later producing measurable inbreeding and loss of genetic variation.
The US Fur Products Labeling Act was enacted, requiring fur labels to name the animal and country of origin.
The Truth in Fur Labeling Act ended the US labeling exemption for items with less than 150 US dollars of fur.
The European Commission responded to the Fur Free Europe citizens' initiative by requesting an EFSA opinion before deciding next steps.
California's ban on selling and manufacturing new fur products took effect on 1 January.
Norway's ban on fur farming took effect in February after a compensated phase-out.
EFSA identified locomotory disorders in Arctic foxes and group stress in red foxes among welfare consequences of current cages.
